pressure.title: Corona charging and collection
pressure.description: A high negative DC voltage on the discharge wires ionises the gas (corona). Dust particles pick up charge and drift to the earthed plates, where they collect. Periodic rapping drops the dust layer into the hoppers. ESPs reach very high efficiencies (typically > 99.5 %); dust resistivity, gas temperature and flow distribution govern performance. Recovered alumina is returned to product.

video_tutorials.title: Alumina Dust Collection System — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Alumina Dust Collection System.
An electrostatic precipitator (ESP) removes alumina dust from calciner off-gas.
High-voltage discharge electrodes charge the dust particles, which drift to earthed collecting plates.
Rappers knock the dust into hoppers and it is returned to product.
Typical applications include calciner and kiln off-gas cleaning; power-plant fly ash.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Casing, Inlet/Outlet Transitions (with gas distribution) & Dust Hoppers.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

video_tutorials.title: Alumina Dust Collection System — Operation

script.narration: How the Alumina Dust Collection System works.
Dusty gas enters through the distribution screens.
Discharge electrodes create a corona.
Charged dust collects on plates.
Rappers drop it into hoppers.
The T/R set supplies HV.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.
A high negative DC voltage on the discharge wires ionises the gas (corona).

video_tutorials.title: Alumina Dust Collection System — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Alumina Dust Collection System.
Monitor spark rate, voltage, current.
Check rappers and hopper evacuation.
Internal inspection; electrode repair.
Watch for back-corona: low efficiency. Common cause: high dust resistivity.
Watch for broken electrode: short circuit, field trip. Common cause: fatigue.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
